faq.q: How far is Estepona from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Estepona is about 15–20 km west of Puerto Banús, a 20–30 minute drive or a 30–40 minute boat ride. All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, so you'll need to travel there to board. The scenic coastline makes the short trip worthwhile.

faq.q: Can I charter a boat for a half-day recovery trip?
faq.a: Yes. Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are available from 2 hours (€749) up to 8 hours (€2,299). For Ironman recovery, a 4-hour cruise is popular – enough time to swim, sunbathe, and enjoy snacks without overdoing it.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, 21% IVA, and a selection of drinks (water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava) plus light snacks. You just need to bring swimwear, sunscreen, and your post-race appetite.

faq.q: Are there boats with jet skis for post-race fun?
faq.a: Yes. Our Tier B boats – the Mangusta 80 (white and grey variants) – include a free jet ski for your charter. Minimum booking is 4 hours at €4,719. It's a great way to add some adrenaline after the Ironman.

faq.q: Can I book a boat for a large group of Ironman supporters?
faq.a: Absolutely. Our largest yachts (Ferretti 94, Canados 86, Maiora 26m) accommodate up to 12 guests. For bigger groups, you can charter multiple boats. Contact us via WhatsApp to discuss availability and pricing for your party.

faq.q: What is the best time of day for a recovery cruise?
faq.a: Afternoon charters (12:00–18:00) are ideal – the sea is warm, the sun is high, and you can watch the sunset on your return. Morning trips are calmer and cooler. We recommend booking at least 3–4 hours to fully unwind.

faq.q: Do I need to bring my own food and drinks?
faq.a: No, we provide water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. You're welcome to bring your own food or special treats – just let us know in advance. The skipper can suggest good spots to anchor for a swim.

faq.q: How do I book an Estepona boat charter for Ironman 2034?
faq.a: Simply contact us via WhatsApp with your preferred date, boat type, and duration. We'll confirm availability and send you a booking link. For Tier A and Tier B boats, prices are fixed; for others, we'll provide a custom quote.

data.body_html:
After crossing the Ironman 2034 finish line in Estepona, your muscles deserve a break. A private Estepona boat charter for Ironman 2034 recovery day offers the perfect blend of relaxation, gentle movement, and sea air. Depart from Puerto Banús, just 20 minutes east, and cruise the Costa del Sol aboard one of our fleet. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance – so you can focus on nothing but the horizon. Prices start at €749 for 2 hours on an Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 (up to 9 guests). For larger groups, our 12-metre-plus yachts (Mangusta 80, Ferretti 94, Canados 86) accommodate up to 12 people. Book via WhatsApp for custom durations.

Why choose a boat charter for Ironman recovery?

Recovery after an Ironman is as important as the race itself. Floating on the Mediterranean reduces muscle tension, lowers cortisol, and promotes blood flow – all without the impact of running or cycling. A gentle cruise along the coast from Estepona to Cabopino or Cala del Faro lets you soak up vitamin D and magnesium-rich sea air. You can swim in calm coves, stretch on deck, and enjoy light snacks and drinks provided onboard. No gym, no pavement – just the rhythm of the waves.

Our fleet for your recovery day

We offer a range of boats to suit your group size and budget. All depart from Puerto Banús, a 20–30 minute drive from Estepona. Here's a quick overview:

  • Tier A (€749/2h – €2,299/8h): Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax). Ideal for small groups. Includes skipper, drinks, snacks, VAT.
  • Tier B (€4,719 minimum 4h): Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) in white or grey. Includes a free jet ski – perfect for a post-race adrenaline boost.
  • Other boats (pricing on request): From the speedy Pershing 46 to the spacious Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax). Contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote.

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%).

Sample itinerary: Estepona to Cala Cortés

A typical 4-hour recovery cruise might look like this: depart Puerto Banús at 14:00, head west past the Golden Mile and Marbella's beaches. Stop for a swim at Cala del Faro, a quiet cove with crystal-clear water. Continue to Cala Cortés, where you can anchor for 45 minutes – float, stretch, and enjoy a cava toast. On the return, cruise past the marina at Estepona (you'll see the finish line from the water) and arrive back at Puerto Banús by 18:00. If you want to extend, an 8-hour charter lets you reach Cabopino or even Sotogrande.

What to bring and what's provided

We've got the essentials covered: skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance. You just need swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (SPF 50+), a hat, and sunglasses. If you're still sore from the race, bring a light jacket for the breeze. You're welcome to bring your own food – perhaps a post-race picnic. The skipper will have cool boxes and ice. For music, most boats have Bluetooth speakers – bring your playlist of chill tunes.

Booking your Estepona boat charter for Ironman 2034

Ready to book? Contact us on WhatsApp with your preferred date, boat type, and duration. We'll confirm availability and send a booking link. For Tier A and Tier B boats, prices are fixed; for others, we'll provide a custom quote. Book early – Ironman week sees high demand. You can also browse all our Marbella boat charters for more inspiration. We recommend a 4-hour charter (€1,299 on Tier A) for a relaxed recovery afternoon.
